quest.title: Words Worth Their Weight in Mora
quest.description: The recent crisis that beset Liyue Harbor has reinvigorated interest in history. Wanwen Bookhouse has seen a resurgence in business as a result, and its owner Jifang is on the verge of being overwhelmed...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Mora x15000, Teachings of Prosperity x4, Teachings of Diligence x4, Teachings of Gold x4

dialogues.speaker: Gentry De'an
dialogues.text: What is it, youngster?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here's the order you placed with Jifang.

dialogues.speaker: Gentry De'an
dialogues.text: The fourth volume of Rex Incognito? I placed this order eons ago. Why has it tarried till now?

dialogues.speaker: Gentry De'an
dialogues.text: Let me see. Huh? A first edition? Why, no wonder it took so long...

dialogues.speaker: Gentry De'an
dialogues.text: To think I'd assumed that Jifang had forgotten about my book amid all the other customers...

dialogues.speaker: Gentry De'an
dialogues.text: Thank you for delivering this book to me, youngster.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Tian
dialogues.text: What can I do for you, youngster?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here's the order you placed with Jifang.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Tian
dialogues.text: The what now? ...Oh, ah yes. I believe I ordered a copy of the Verses of Equilibrium at the Wanwen Bookhouse.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Tian
dialogues.text: Indeed, indeed, this is the book that I wanted. Haha, I was beginning to think that Jifang might have forgotten about my order, what with the other customers and all...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Tian
dialogues.text: But it's here now, and that's good. The binding is fairly good as well. Conscientious as always, that Jifang.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Tian
dialogues.text: Thank you, youngster. I'll take this with me, now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about those two books...

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: Have you delivered them?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, I have.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: Thank you. Wanwen Bookhouse has managed to stay open all this time due to the support of our long-time customers.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: What's more, these customers are true lovers of books. It should gladden them greatly to receive good ones.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: Thanks so much for your help, Traveler. Please take this as compensation for your efforts.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: If you should ever wish to purchase any books, feel free to approach me.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: So, about those two books...

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: The two of them are long-time customers of ours. I usually prepare their books beforehand.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: But I ended up dragging my feet a little this time due to the surge in business.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: They must have gotten impatient...

dialogues.speaker: Gentry De'an
dialogues.text: Alas, Rex Lapis...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Tian
dialogues.text: "They who read history shall learn how we rise and fall..." So they say, but there are few who read history to learn these things nowadays...
